providers.reason: GE Vernova enters its October 28 earnings report with strong momentum from a $176 billion backlog and a 5% rebound on October 26. Surging demand for gas turbines and grid equipment, particularly from AI data centers, provides high multi-year visibility. Technical indicators show the stock recovering from oversold levels near the $800 support.
providers.risk: Earnings-day volatility if management fails to significantly raise guidance to justify current valuation multiples.

providers.reason: The October 28 premarket report is a near-term catalyst: consensus expects about $4.03 EPS on $12.1B revenue, while a new US wind-import order favors GEV. Shares rebounded 4.9% on October 26 after a sharp AI-infrastructure selloff, supporting a pre-event long.
providers.risk: A miss or soft margin/cash-flow outlook—GEV already missed Q2 EPS—could trigger another double-digit de-rating; the earnings event is binary.

providers.reason: Q3 earnings tomorrow with $176B backlog and 20% revenue growth expected. Recent 11% drop on Meta AI financing concerns creates bounce potential. Data center orders exceeded $5B in H1 2026, electrification backlog surged to $42B.
providers.risk: Wind segment losing $400M EBITDA in 2026 and Q2 adjusted EPS miss raise profitability concerns. Meta-driven AI financing fears could persist post-earnings.

providers.reason: Rebounded ~5% Oct. 26 on gas-power strength and AI data-center power demand; continued gas equipment order strength expected with 17-19% revenue growth.
providers.risk: Ex-dividend Oct. 27 and extended move near $815-$827 with Fed rate sensitivity.
